purpose: Alglucosidase alfa is used to treat Pompe disease, a rare inherited condition where the body cannot break down a sugar called glycogen properly. This causes glycogen to build up in your muscles, making them weak over time. This medicine helps slow down or stop that muscle damage.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes an enzyme called GAA that breaks down glycogen in your cells. In Pompe disease, your body either makes little or none of this enzyme. This medicine is a man-made version of that enzyme, and when it is given to you through an IV, it goes into your cells and does the job your body cannot do on its own.
common_side_effects: Flushing, rash, or hives during or after the infusion. You may also experience headache, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, fever, or feeling tired. Some people have muscle aches or changes in heart rate during treatment.
warnings: Serious allergic reactions, including life-threatening anaphylaxis, can happen during the infusion, so you will always be monitored closely. There is also a risk of severe heart and breathing problems, especially in infants. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, swelling, or feel very unwell. Do not stop treatment without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an IV infusion (a drip into your vein) in a clinic or hospital setting. The usual dose is 20 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given once every two weeks. Each infusion takes several hours, and staff will watch you carefully during and after the treatment.
